facts.t: The Vice-President's casting vote has been used once in memory
facts.d: In 1972 Vice-President G. S. Pathak broke a tie on the Payment of Bonus Bill. Party dominance in the Rajya Sabha makes exact ties almost impossible — unlike the American Senate, where the Vice-President's tie-breaking vote is a routine instrument of government.

facts.t: Britain has no Vice-President at all
facts.d: Succession runs from the monarch, and government leadership from the Prime Minister. France has no permanent Vice-President either — the President of the Senate stands in. Only India and the United States maintain a standing deputy head of state.

facts.t: States do not vote for the Chairman of the Council of States
facts.d: The Vice-President is elected by an electoral college of MPs from both Houses. No MLA participates — even though the office presides over the chamber that exists to represent the states.

bank.q: With reference to the election of the Vice-President, consider the following statements:
s: The electoral college consists of members of both Houses of Parliament.
Members of state legislative assemblies participate.
bank.e: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Unlike the presidential election, nominated members vote — but states do not participate at all.

bank.q: The last recorded use of the Vice-President's casting vote in India was on:
bank.e: Vice-President G. S. Pathak's tie-breaking vote in 1972. Party dominance makes exact ties vanishingly rare.

bank.q: Match List I (episode) with List II (Vice-President and year):
pairs: A. Rejection of the impeachment motion against CJI Dipak Misra
B. Admitting the FDI in retail discussion
C. Suspension of twelve Opposition MPs
D. Refusal of the Pegasus motion under Rule 267
bank.e: Naidu on the impeachment motion in 2018 and the suspensions in 2021, Ansari on FDI in 2012, and Dhankhar on Pegasus in 2023.

bank.q: Which one of the following is NOT identified as a weakness of the office?
o: It has no substantive powers except when acting as President
It has no electoral link with the states
It is first in the line of presidential succession
bank.e: Succession is a strength — it ensures the Presidency never falls vacant.

bank.as: The Vice-President's federal legitimacy is described as weaker than the President's.
bank.rs: The President is elected by an electoral college that includes state legislators, while the Vice-President is not.
bank.e: Both true and the Reason explains the Assertion — hence the proposal to include state legislatures in the electoral college at lower weightage.

bank.q: Consider the following statements comparing the Indian and American Vice-Presidencies:
s: Both preside over the upper chamber and hold a tie-breaking vote.
The American Vice-President holds substantive executive authority in the Cabinet and the National Security Council.
The Indian Vice-President is expected to be politically neutral.
bank.e: All three are correct. The Indian office has no executive role unless acting as President — the sharpest structural difference between the two.

bank.q: Under which rule did Vice-President Dhankhar disallow short-duration discussions in 2023?
bank.e: Rule 267, which governs suspension of business. Rule 256 concerns suspension of members and Rule 266 the interpretation of rules.

bank.q: All of the following are proposed reforms for the office EXCEPT:
o: A code of impartial conduct for the Chair
Suspension of active party membership on assuming office
Making the Vice-President a voting member of the Cabinet
An annual State of Rajya Sabha Report on productivity and legislative quality
bank.e: That would import the American model and destroy the neutrality the Indian office is built on. The proposals aim to strengthen impartiality, not executive involvement.

bank.q: With reference to the Chair's federal role, consider the following:
s: During the 2016 GST debate the Chair ensured Tamil Nadu and West Bengal concerns were heard, contributing to compensation guarantees.
The federal voice of the Chair is often dominated by party whips.
The Chair may vote on ordinary legislation like any other member.
bank.e: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. The Chair votes only in the event of a tie — the casting vote — and not otherwise.

bank.q: Which country has no office of Vice-President and no permanent equivalent?
bank.e: The United Kingdom. France also lacks a permanent Vice-President, with the President of the Senate standing in for succession.
